<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  /* Reading mode hides the chrome and the empty .arxiv-html-header marker: the pinned JS reads
     the marker's display to know which way to toggle. The marker draws no box. */
  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }
  html[data-reading-mode="enabled"] :is(.arxiv-html-site-chrome, .arxiv-html-header, .ds-site-footer) { display: none; }
  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }
    .arxiv-html-footer { padding-inline: 1rem; }
  }

<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Zifei Wang<sup id="id1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1,∗</span></sup></span>
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Wei Wen<sup id="id2" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">2,∗†</span></sup>
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Qiang Ji<sup id="id3" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1</span></sup>
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Qian-Wen Zhang<sup id="id4" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1,2</span></sup>
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Ruizhi Qiao<sup id="id5" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">2</span></sup>
</span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">He Liu<sup id="id6" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1</span></sup>

<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">

<span class="ltx_personname">Qiang Lin<sup id="id8" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">2</span></sup>
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span><sup id="id9" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">1</span></sup>Tencent IMA Product Center  <sup id="id10" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">2</span></sup>Tencent Youtu Lab
</span></span></span></span></div>
<div class="ltx_dates">November 19, 2026</div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Multimodal retrieval now has to match dense pages, fine-grained entities, ordered video, and the tools and memory an agent looks up. A single vector drops the local evidence that decides these matches. A cross-encoder can recover it, but only by rereading every recalled page or clip. Late interaction keeps the evidence in the index; storing every token vector is too large to serve. OmniEVIE is a 4.5B multi-vector embedding model that covers text, images, visual documents, video, and tools with one compressed index and a three-stage retriever. Each record holds at most <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> int8 vectors of dimension <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math>: <math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9{,}472" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9,472</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9{,}472</annotation></semantics></math> bytes per record, or <math id="abstract1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8.82</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.82</annotation></semantics></math> GiB per million records. Retrieval runs on that compressed index, and a returned hit names the page region or the video interval. Training, merging, indexing, and retrieval are designed together. Every task is written as one retrieval sample. A three-grade evidence check removes false negatives, and the sampling rate follows the gap between the baseline and the teachers. Candidates are compressed with ST-HAC during training, in the form stored in the index, so the training score and the serving score use the same vectors. Stage-wise runs and specialist branches are merged by parameter block. A saliency gate and a noise floor rewrite the query score. One compressed record supplies a mean vector, <math id="abstract1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>-bit signs, and int8 multi-vectors, used for the coarse, middle, and final stages. Trained on public datasets, the full sequence at <math id="abstract1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math> scores <math id="abstract1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.68" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.68</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.68</annotation></semantics></math> on MMEB-V3 (190 tasks), and the <math id="abstract1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K128\times d64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K128\times d64</annotation></semantics></math> int8 index scores <math id="abstract1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.06</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.06</annotation></semantics></math>. The same compressed index scores <math id="abstract1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="77.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>77.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">77.96</annotation></semantics></math> on MMEB-V2 (78 tasks) and <math id="abstract1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="62.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>62.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62.96</annotation></semantics></math> on ViDoRe V3 (48 tasks). On corpora of <math id="abstract1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> million and <math id="abstract1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> million records, one single-thread query takes <math id="abstract1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="54.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>54.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54.2</annotation></semantics></math> ms and <math id="abstract1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="120.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>120.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">120.2</annotation></semantics></math> ms, <math id="abstract1.m16" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="11.1\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>11.1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11.1\times</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="abstract1.m17" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="25.3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25.3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25.3\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster than exact search over <math id="abstract1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4096</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4096</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional single vectors, and <math id="abstract1.m19" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="236\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>236</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">236\times</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="abstract1.m20" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="532\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>532</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">532\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster than full int8 MaxSim. Video is encoded directly from frames and a hit is read back to its start and end in seconds, so neither indexing nor localization uses a video parsing model. On the <math id="abstract1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}083" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,083</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}083</annotation></semantics></math> queries of the QVHighlights validation set, the heat peak falls inside the labeled segment for <math id="abstract1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="78.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>78.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> of them and the returned span intersects it for <math id="abstract1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>94.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">94.3\%</annotation></semantics></math>, against <math id="abstract1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="44.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>44.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">44.9\%</annotation></semantics></math> for a random span of the same length; the span covers <math id="abstract1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>18</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the video on average. Weights and code are at <a href="https://huggingface.co/tencent/OmniEVIE-4B" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://huggingface.co/tencent/OmniEVIE-4B</a> and <a href="https://github.com/Tencent/OmniEVIE" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/Tencent/OmniEVIE</a>.</p>
  
</div><span id="footnotex1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnotetext"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">footnotetext: </span>Equal contribution.</span></span></span><span id="footnotex2" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnotetext"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">2</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">footnotetext: </span>Corresponding author. Contact: <span id="footnotex2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">jawnrwen@tencent.com</span>.</span></span></span>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<section id="S1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">1.1 </span>From a single vector to multi-vector retrieval</h3>

<div id="S1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Retrieval queries now include multi-page reports, fine-grained products and landmarks, long videos with ordered actions, and agent contexts built from tool descriptions, interface state, and multi-step history <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>. Relevance often depends on a few non-adjacent pieces of evidence: a header and one cell in a financial table, the order of two actions in a video, or one parameter in a long tool document.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A single <math id="S1.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional vector scores a query and a candidate by one inner product. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Weller et al. [36]</a></cite> show that this score can place only some combinations first: past a corpus size that grows polynomially with <math id="S1.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, a document that must be recognized by several pieces at once cannot be ranked first by any query. Adding data or enlarging the backbone does not remove that limit.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Late interaction keeps a query token set <math id="S1.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=\{q_{1},\ldots,q_{L_{q}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=\{q_{1},\ldots,q_{L_{q}}\}</annotation></semantics></math> and a candidate set <math id="S1.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=\{v_{1},\ldots,v_{K}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=\{v_{1},\ldots,v_{K}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, and scores each query token by its best match in the candidate <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>, <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>:</p>
<table id="S1.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{MaxSim}(Q,D)=\sum_{i=1}^{L_{q}}w_{i}\max_{1\leq j\leq K}\langle q_{i},v_{j}\rangle," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>MaxSim</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{MaxSim}(Q,D)=\sum_{i=1}^{L_{q}}w_{i}\max_{1\leq j\leq K}\langle q_{i},v_{j}\rangle,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="S1.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{i}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{i}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. Because each query token can land on a different span, the score is no longer limited by the dimension of one vector. The leading visual-document and text-to-video retrievers use this form <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>, <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">1.2 </span>Three obstacles at serving time</h3>

<div id="S1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">That representation is expensive to serve, for three separate reasons. A high-resolution page or a clip of tens of seconds produces thousands of vectors, so a million records occupy hundreds of gigabytes in floating point. A query then has to be compared with every vector: one single-thread query on a million-record corpus takes on the order of ten seconds. Failure modes also differ across documents, images, video, and tools: upweighting one modality often degrades the others, and a model trained on the full token sequence loses accuracy once those tokens are compressed for the index.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">1.3 </span>What OmniEVIE does</h3>

<div id="S1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The usual compromise retrieves with one vector and reranks with a cross-encoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>, <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite>. Each of the <math id="S1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> recalled pages or clips is forwarded again with the query, so the system has to read the raw media online. An uncompressed multi-vector index has the opposite problem: prior studies show that MaxSim selects only about <math id="S1.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the stored vectors <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>. OmniEVIE keeps the width at <math id="S1.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\leq 128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\leq 128</annotation></semantics></math>, bounds the number of vectors, and stores them at low bit width. Search runs on that compressed index (Table <a href="#S1.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 1.3 What OmniEVIE does ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The model extends the evidence check and the local multi-vector index of EVIE from visual documents to general multimodal retrieval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>. A mined candidate stays a negative only when it lacks the evidence the query asks for. Position codes guide clustering and are then discarded, so the index stores semantic centroids. The same integer record is what the retriever filters and what it uses to name the hit. This release is trained on <math id="S1.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>57</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57</annotation></semantics></math> public datasets. The changes are in the backbone, the order in which modalities are added, and the decision to train on the same clustered vectors that are written to the index.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A hit also carries the place of its evidence. A page or an image returns the bounding rectangle of the hit clusters, and a video returns the start and end in seconds of the hit centroids, so the downstream generator reads that region or that span instead of the whole page or video. The video side encodes the sampled frames directly and takes time from the frame indices, so neither indexing nor localization goes through a parsing model that transcribes video into text. The localization numbers are in Section <a href="#S9.SS5" title="9.5 Evidence localization and video time localization ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9.5</span></a>. Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1.3 What OmniEVIE does ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> shows the resulting accuracy and latency, and Table <a href="#S1.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 1.3 What OmniEVIE does ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> compares the four serving designs.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.32203v1/figures/fig1_overview.png" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/202;" width="476" height="202" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span>Accuracy and latency of OmniEVIE. (a) MMEB-V3 mean over 190 tasks against parameter scale. The blue line is the full sequence at <math id="S1.F1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math>: the same weights keep every token vector, with no ST-HAC and no int8 quantization, and score <math id="S1.F1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.68" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.68</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.68</annotation></semantics></math>. The circle and the diamond are the released <math id="S1.F1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K128\times d64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K128\times d64</annotation></semantics></math> int8 index, <math id="S1.F1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8.82</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.82</annotation></semantics></math> GiB per million records, at <math id="S1.F1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.06</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.06</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S1.F1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> frames and <math id="S1.F1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="59.76" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>59.76</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">59.76</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S1.F1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> frames. WeMM-Embedding-4B and OmniEVIE share a <math id="S1.F1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.5</annotation></semantics></math>B backbone. (b) Single-thread latency against corpus size for full int8 MaxSim, exact single-vector search at <math id="S1.F1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.F1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=4096</annotation></semantics></math>, and the three-stage retriever, whose first stage is a <math id="S1.F1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=64</annotation></semantics></math> mean vector.</figcaption>
</figure>

</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S1.T1.4.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S1.T1.4.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">
<span id="S1.T1.4.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:55.2pt;">
<span id="S1.T1.4.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.T1.4.4.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">Million-scale index</span></span>

</table>
</figure>
<div id="S1.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The rest of the report follows that record from training to search. Section <a href="#S3" title="3 Training data ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> writes retrieval, classification, question answering, grounding, and tool use as one sample, grades the evidence in mined negatives, and adds video negatives that differ only in order. Section <a href="#S4" title="4 Model and training ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> trains a bidirectional backbone with native video tokens and one Prefix-MRL head for widths <math id="S1.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> through <math id="S1.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2048</annotation></semantics></math>; clustering during training and the query-side score are in that section. Section <a href="#S5" title="5 Block-wise model merging ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> adds stage-wise and specialist checkpoints by parameter block. Section <a href="#S6" title="6 ST-HAC ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> uses one spatiotemporal clustering for every modality; the bytes in one record are given there. Section <a href="#S7" title="7 Three-stage retrieval ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> derives three representations from one record and narrows the candidate window. Section <a href="#S7.SS5" title="7.5 Localizing the hit ‣ 7 Three-stage retrieval ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.5</span></a> reads the hit back to a page rectangle or to seconds in a video without a video parsing model. The numbers are in Section <a href="#S9.SS5" title="9.5 Evidence localization and video time localization ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9.5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related work</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>General multimodal embeddings and multi-vector representations</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">One general embedding model is now expected to handle text, images, documents, and video. VLM2Vec and the MMEB suites put retrieval, classification, question answering, and grounding into one evaluation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Esfandiarpoor et al. [5]</a></cite> measure what that similarity score costs once the query needs several pieces of evidence. Qwen3-VL-Embedding, WeMM-Embedding, Ovis-Embedding, and U-MARVEL train a single vector with multi-stage contrastive learning, hard negatives, reranker supervision, and cross-scale distillation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>, <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>, <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>, <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite>. By contrast, jina-embeddings-v4 and v5-omni keep both a single vector and a multi-vector output, and lock the vision tower so the geometry stays aligned <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>, <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Late interaction was established for text by ColBERT and ColBERTv2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>, <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>]</cite> and carried to full-page visual documents by ColPali, which replaces an OCR pipeline with a page screenshot <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>. ViDoRe V3 extends that evaluation to multilingual pages <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite>. Jina-ColBERT-v2 covers multilingual text <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>. ModernVBERT and Nemotron-ColEmbed-V2 study bidirectional attention and model merging for document late interaction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>, <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>. Video-ColBERT and CLAMR extend late interaction to video <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite>. EVIE applies evidence checking, a Prefix-MRL head, and layout-aware HAC to visual documents <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>. Matryoshka representation learning and MatFormer nest several widths in one forward pass <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>, <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>. MetaEmbed changes the number of meta-tokens at test time <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>. OmniEVIE carries this design to images, video, text, and agent tasks, and adds a shared spatiotemporal compression, block-wise merging, query-side scoring, and million-scale three-stage retrieval.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Compression and fast multi-vector search</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Compressing a multi-vector index is a choice of which part of the match to keep. MUVERA replaces MaxSim by one fixed-dimensional vector so that an existing maximum-inner-product index can be reused <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>. PLAID keeps the multi-vector score but filters through a global codebook and residual codes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>]</cite>, and query-aware token budgeting delays the choice of raw tokens until the final stage <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite>. A third line reduces the number of stored vectors, either by merging tokens inside the encoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite> or by clustering and pruning a frozen index, as in attention-guided clustering <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>, MarginMerge <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite>, and prune-then-merge <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite>. ST-HAC belongs to this third line, with one difference: the same clustering is used while training and again when the index is written. The mean, the <math id="S2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>-bit signs, and the int8 multi-vectors are then three readings of that one record, at a fixed int8 scale.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.3 </span>False negatives, rank distillation, and model merging</h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The quality of a contrastive embedding depends on which negatives are false and on whose ranking is distilled. FALCON studies false negatives in large-scale image-text pretraining <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>. CORE distills a reranker ranking into an embedding with Rank-KL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite>. On the parameter side, task arithmetic adds and subtracts task vectors <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>, and TIES-Merging drops small deltas and resolves sign conflicts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite>. Conan-embedding-v3, PlaM, and training-free mitigation study modality-specific fusion, layer-selective injection, and the recovery of language ability after multimodal tuning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>, <a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>, <a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite>. The merge in OmniEVIE gives each parameter block its own coefficient, so the merger and the projection head can take a different step from the language layers.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Training data</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OmniEVIE puts every task into one retrieval sample. The instruction says which task it is, the evidence grade says whether a mined negative is truly negative, and a dynamic sampling rule adjusts how often each sample is revisited.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>One sample format</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each example is</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{i}=\big(I_{i},\,q_{i},\,d_{i}^{+},\,\mathcal{N}_{i},\,y_{i}\big)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{i}=\big(I_{i},\,q_{i},\,d_{i}^{+},\,\mathcal{N}_{i},\,y_{i}\big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is a scene instruction, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is text, an image, an image-text pair, or a video, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> is the positive, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{N}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{N}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is a set of explicit hard negatives, and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is a teacher score or a distribution. Retrieval and grounding use the page, image, crop, or clip as the positive. Classification uses the class name as a candidate and prefers near-miss classes from the same dataset, balanced by class frequency. Open question answering pairs the question and the image with the reference answer. Multiple choice uses the correct option as the positive and the other options as hard negatives. Tool retrieval uses the tool document or skill description as the candidate. Interface and memory tasks are held out for zero-shot evaluation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A batch contains one task, so every in-batch negative is another candidate of that task. The training mixture comprises about <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>M samples from <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>57</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57</annotation></semantics></math> public datasets (Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.1 One sample format ‣ 3 Training data ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.32203v1/fig_data_dist.svg" id="S3.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/213;" width="476" height="213"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span>Training mixture across <math id="S3.F2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>57</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57</annotation></semantics></math> public datasets (about <math id="S3.F2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>M samples). (a) Sample share by task family: image retrieval <math id="S3.F2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25.8\%</annotation></semantics></math>, QA and grounding <math id="S3.F2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>24.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24.9\%</annotation></semantics></math>, text retrieval <math id="S3.F2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15.6\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>15.6</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15.6\%</annotation></semantics></math>, classification <math id="S3.F2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>13.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13.5\%</annotation></semantics></math>, video retrieval <math id="S3.F2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>13.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>, tool retrieval <math id="S3.F2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5.2</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.2\%</annotation></semantics></math>, and visual documents <math id="S3.F2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>. (b) Dataset count and query-to-candidate mapping per family; visual documents are replayed from stage 1.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Scene instructions</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Image-to-image search takes the instruction, the image, and an empty text span as the query. Composed search places the real question after the image. A text query places the instruction in front of the question, and the remaining zero-shot tasks share one task prefix (Table <a href="#S3.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 3.2 Scene instructions ‣ 3 Training data ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). Very thin or very small images are resized on the short side and padded so that the aspect ratio stays bounded.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Evidence grades and temporal hard negatives</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">High-scoring mined candidates are the usual source of hard negatives, and they are also where missed positives hide. If a page that answers the query is treated as a negative, the gradient pushes that page away from the query. A multimodal judge assigns each mined negative one of three grades (Table <a href="#S3.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 3.3 Evidence grades and temporal hard negatives ‣ 3 Training data ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). Candidates with full evidence are promoted to positives (each receiving weight <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega_{i}=1/n_{i}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msubsup><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega_{i}=1/n_{i}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> when a query has <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{i}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{i}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> positives), those with partial evidence are masked in the loss denominator, and those with no evidence remain hard negatives.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>Three-grade evidence check on the visual-document pool. Counts are candidate negatives before the grade is applied.</figcaption>
<table id="S3.T3.4" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S3.T3.4.1" class="ltx_tr">

</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Static background is often enough to recognize a clip, so two hard negatives put the loss on temporal order. A reversed negative pairs a forward clip (positive) with the same clip in reverse, and the query pairs a forward description with a reversed one. An off-window negative keeps the target span as the positive and takes another span of the same long video as the negative, under the original query.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Dynamic sampling from a baseline and several teachers</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Not every sample deserves the same update. Some are already solved by the baseline, and on some tasks every available teacher is weak. The teacher is chosen by the form of the answer. Open answers and fine-grained classification use a multimodal embedding teacher and its in-batch similarity distribution. Ranking tasks, including text-to-image, video grounding, and tool retrieval, use a cross-encoder and the gaps among candidates. Multiple choice uses a discriminative teacher and the distribution over options.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Each sample is then labeled by whether the baseline and the teacher place the positive first (Table <a href="#S3.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 3.4 Dynamic sampling from a baseline and several teachers ‣ 3 Training data ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). Samples that both models rank correctly by a wide margin are downsampled. Samples the teacher ranks correctly and the baseline misses are upweighted. When the baseline beats the teacher, distillation is turned off and the loss uses the gold label. If the baseline outperforms the teacher on more samples of a task than the reverse, distillation is turned off for that task.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 4: </span>Five-way sample policy. “First” means the positive is ranked first. Distillation is on only when the teacher is correct.</figcaption>
<table id="S3.T4.4" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">

<span id="S3.T4.4.5.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:38.0pt;">

</span></td>
<td id="S3.T4.4.5.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">

</span></td>
<td id="S3.T4.4.5.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">

</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T4.4.6" class="ltx_tr">

</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Model and training</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Backbone, bidirectional attention, and native video</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OmniEVIE is built on the Qwen3.5-VL mixed-attention backbone: a vision encoder, a cross-modal merger, language layers, and a Prefix-MRL head. The released model has <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.5</annotation></semantics></math>B parameters and hidden width <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{hid}}=2560" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>hid</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2560</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{hid}}=2560</annotation></semantics></math>. Language layers alternate GatedDeltaNet blocks and full attention. The document stage distills an <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>B bidirectional EVIE teacher with <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\mathrm{hid}}=4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>hid</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\mathrm{hid}}=4096</annotation></semantics></math> into this <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.5</annotation></semantics></math>B model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Text is embedded by the tokenizer. Images and pages become patch tokens after the vision encoder and a spatial merge. A causal mask would hide a later instruction from the visual tokens that precede it. Full-attention layers use bidirectional attention, and the mask marks padding. Linear-attention blocks stay as in the backbone. Every token can then attend over the full sequence <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>, <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>, <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">OmniEVIE feeds each clip as one sequence, so adjacent frames meet inside the encoder. Per-frame encoding instead runs one forward per frame and pools the vectors afterward, so frames meet only after the backbone, a reversed clip yields the same set of frames, and exceeding the token budget forces dropping frames. Adjacent frames are packed at the vision-encoder input with temporal stride <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta t_{\mathrm{patch}}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>patch</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta t_{\mathrm{patch}}=2</annotation></semantics></math>, and the last frame is repeated when the count is odd. Each temporal group is prefixed by a timestamp in seconds. When the token budget is exceeded, every frame is scaled down by the same factor and the time samples stay. Timestamps increase with position, so a reversed clip pairs content with a different timestamp, and the reversed negatives of Section <a href="#S3" title="3 Training data ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> have a nonzero gradient.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Prefix-MRL</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Distillation needs a wide vector, and the index needs a narrow one. One shared matrix <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W\in\mathbb{R}^{2048\times 2560}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>2048</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2560</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W\in\mathbb{R}^{2048\times 2560}</annotation></semantics></math> sits on top of the backbone. For a final hidden state <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathbb{R}^{2560}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>2560</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathbb{R}^{2560}</annotation></semantics></math> and a width <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\in\mathcal{D}=\{64,128,256,512,1024,2048\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>64,128,256,512</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1024</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\in\mathcal{D}=\{64,128,256,512,1024,2048\}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S4.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="e^{(d)}(h)=\operatorname{L2}\!\left(W_{:d}\,h\right)=\frac{W_{:d}\,h}{\|W_{:d}\,h\|_{2}}\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mpadded style="width:1.011em;" width="1.011em"><mi>L2</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>W</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mi>h</mi></mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>W</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em">∥</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{(d)}(h)=\operatorname{L2}\!\left(W_{:d}\,h\right)=\frac{W_{:d}\,h}{\|W_{:d}\,h\|_{2}}\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">A single forward pass produces every width, and a low-width loss updates only the first <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> rows. Serving always stores <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=64</annotation></semantics></math>, while the <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math> branch provides the high-width reference for self-distillation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Four training stages</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Training every modality from scratch in one stage lets frequent easy tasks crowd out the harder alignment, and adding a modality later can erase the document behavior already learned. OmniEVIE adds modalities in four stages (Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.3 Four training stages ‣ 4 Model and training ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.3 Four training stages ‣ 4 Model and training ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) and replays earlier data at a fixed rate. Each batch is still a single task.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.32203v1/figures/fig2_training.png" id="S4.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/311;" width="476" height="311" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Four-stage schedule and the forward graph. (a) The curriculum and the four specialist branches split off after stage 3. (b) Vision, instruction, and text pass through the backbone and the Prefix-MRL head, then split into a <math id="S4.F3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math> reference branch and a <math id="S4.F3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=64</annotation></semantics></math> serving branch. The query keeps its full sequence, and stage 4 attaches the gate and the noise floor. Candidates are clustered with ST-HAC during training. The <math id="S4.F3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math> branch and an external teacher distill the <math id="S4.F3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=64</annotation></semantics></math> branch.</figcaption>
</figure>

<tr id="S4.T5.4.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S4.T5.4.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">
<span id="S4.T5.4.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:62.1pt;">

</span></td>

</span></td>
<td id="S4.T5.4.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">
