rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>δ</mi><mi>b</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(\theta)\approx\mathcal{L}(P)+\sum_{b}\Big(a_{b}\,c_{b}+\frac{1}{2}h_{b}\,c_{b}^{2}\Big),\qquad a_{b}=g_{b}^{\top}\delta_{b},\quad h_{b}=\delta_{b}^{\top}H_{bb}\,\delta_{b}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><math id="S5.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{b}&lt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{b}&lt;0</annotation></semantics></math> means the delta reduces the loss, and <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{b}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{b}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> is the curvature cost. Each block is a quadratic in <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{b}</annotation></semantics></math>, with vertex</p>
<table id="S5.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{b}^{\ast}=-\frac{a_{b}}{h_{b}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>b</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{b}^{\ast}=-\frac{a_{b}}{h_{b}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">and the coefficient used is that value clipped to <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. If every block is forced to share a coefficient <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>, the best shared value is the curvature-weighted average of the per-block vertices, and the extra loss is</p>
<table id="S5.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathcal{L}=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{b}h_{b}\big(\bar{c}-c_{b}^{\ast}\big)^{2}\;\geq\;0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>b</mi></munder><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>b</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn> 0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathcal{L}=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{b}h_{b}\big(\bar{c}-c_{b}^{\ast}\big)^{2}\;\geq\;0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.4" class="ltx_p">The gap grows as the per-block optima diverge. The projection head, which writes the stored vectors, has large curvature and a smaller optimal coefficient. The language layers carry most of the task ability and prefer a larger coefficient. A text or tool specialist has <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{b}\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{b}\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> on the vision encoder, so that coefficient is <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>. Trimming removes entries that barely change <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> but inflate <math id="S5.SS2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> and the interference with other specialists. Measured effects of each merge step are in Table <a href="#S8.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ 8.4 Ablations ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>ST-HAC</h2>

<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Agglomerative clustering</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A high-resolution page or a <math id="S6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>-frame clip emits hundreds to thousands of vectors, and they are not spread uniformly. The vectors that Section 1.3 counts as unselected are mostly collinear background and static frames <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>. The evidence that decides a retrieval, a single cell, a small logo, or a short action, is an isolated point far from the background. The compression merges collinear background and static frames into a few clusters, and leaves an isolated piece of evidence in a cluster of its own. Ward clustering merges the pair whose union increases the within-cluster sum of squares the least: nearby background tokens merge first, and an isolated point stays until the end. ST-HAC runs this clustering in a spatiotemporal feature space. Table <a href="#S8.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ 8.5 Compression methods at the same budget ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> compares it with uniform pooling and random pruning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>One procedure for every modality</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After the <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=64</annotation></semantics></math> projection and per-token <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> normalization, any input is a sequence <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\hat{v}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}\subset\mathbb{S}^{d-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\hat{v}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}\subset\mathbb{S}^{d-1}</annotation></semantics></math>. ST-HAC replaces that sequence by at most <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\leq 128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\leq 128</annotation></semantics></math> vectors of dimension <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math>. Figure <a href="#S6.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 6.2 One procedure for every modality ‣ 6 ST-HAC ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> shows the steps. If clustering used semantics alone, similar digits in two columns of a report, or similar backgrounds far apart in a video, would fall into one cluster. Each token therefore receives normalized coordinates <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{i},y_{i},t_{i})\in[0,1]^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{i},y_{i},t_{i})\in[0,1]^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. For a video packed with stride <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta t_{\mathrm{patch}}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>patch</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta t_{\mathrm{patch}}=2</annotation></semantics></math> into <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> groups,</p>
<table id="S6.E16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}=\frac{f_{i}}{\max(F-1,\,1)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn> 1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}=\frac{f_{i}}{\max(F-1,\,1)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">For a text sequence, <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}=(i-1)/\max(N-1,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}=(i-1)/\max(N-1,1)</annotation></semantics></math>. The clustering feature mixes the semantic vector with sinusoidal space and time codes and renormalizes:</p>
<table id="S6.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{i}=\operatorname{L2}\!\Big(w_{v}\,\hat{v}_{i}+w_{s}\,p_{xy}(x_{i},y_{i})+w_{t}\,p_{t}(t_{i})\Big),\qquad w_{v}=1-w_{s}-w_{t}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.011em;" width="1.011em"><mi>L2</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{i}=\operatorname{L2}\!\Big(w_{v}\,\hat{v}_{i}+w_{s}\,p_{xy}(x_{i},y_{i})+w_{t}\,p_{t}(t_{i})\Big),\qquad w_{v}=1-w_{s}-w_{t}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Video uses <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{s},w_{t})=(0.07,0.03)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.07</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.03</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{s},w_{t})=(0.07,0.03)</annotation></semantics></math>. Images and pages use <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0.10,0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0.10,0)</annotation></semantics></math>. Text uses <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,0.10)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.10</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,0.10)</annotation></semantics></math>. A missing axis has weight zero. The code and the output format are shared.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.32203v1/figures/fig4_sthac.png" id="S6.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/232;" width="476" height="232" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span>ST-HAC offline compression. (a)(b) Ward clustering on semantic vectors plus the spatiotemporal code. (c) An isolated region stays its own cluster, and adjacent static frames merge. (d) A centroid is the renormalized mean of the semantic vectors only. (e) Fixed-scale int8. (f) The bytes in one record.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Long inputs are segmented first. Video is cut at <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60</annotation></semantics></math> seconds and text at <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,024</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}024</annotation></semantics></math> tokens. Each segment is clustered, and the segment centroids are clustered again up to <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> with a segment-time code of weight <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{t}=0.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.03</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{t}=0.03</annotation></semantics></math>. The Ward distance matrix then stays inside a segment. Ward clustering on <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{z_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{z_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math> stops at <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> clusters. If <math id="S6.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\leq K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\leq K</annotation></semantics></math>, the full sequence is kept. Position weights are much smaller than the semantic weight, so the partition is still driven by semantics.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>A monotone time code</h3>

<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The spatial code <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{xy}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{xy}</annotation></semantics></math> is a standard multi-frequency sinusoid. The same frequencies are unsafe on time. A frequency above <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> wraps, so two shots that are far apart can receive similar codes. ST-HAC draws <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=d/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=d/2</annotation></semantics></math> frequencies evenly from <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\pi/4,\pi]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\pi/4,\pi]</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S6.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E18.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="p_{t}(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}\big(\sin\omega_{1}t,\ \cos\omega_{1}t,\ \ldots,\ \sin\omega_{M}t,\ \cos\omega_{M}t\big)^{\!\top}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mi>M</mi></msqrt></mfrac><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>sin</mi><msub><mi>ω</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mi>cos</mi><msub><mi>ω</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mi>sin</mi><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mi>cos</mi><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mi>t</mi><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}\big(\sin\omega_{1}t,\ \cos\omega_{1}t,\ \ldots,\ \sin\omega_{M}t,\ \cos\omega_{M}t\big)^{\!\top}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The leading factor is <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/\sqrt{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mi>M</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/\sqrt{M}</annotation></semantics></math>. Each sine–cosine pair then contributes <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/M</annotation></semantics></math> to the squared norm, and <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> pairs give <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|p_{t}(t)\|_{2}^{2}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|p_{t}(t)\|_{2}^{2}=1</annotation></semantics></math>. The inner product of two times separated by <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta t</annotation></semantics></math> is</p>
<table id="S6.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{t}(\Delta t)=\langle p_{t}(t),\,p_{t}(t+\Delta t)\rangle=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^{M}\cos(\omega_{m}\Delta t)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>M</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>M</mi></munderover><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{t}(\Delta t)=\langle p_{t}(t),\,p_{t}(t+\Delta t)\rangle=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^{M}\cos(\omega_{m}\Delta t).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Every <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega_{m}\Delta t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega_{m}\Delta t</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta t\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta t\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> lies in <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,\pi]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,\pi]</annotation></semantics></math>, where cosine decreases, so <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> decreases from <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{t}(0)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{t}(0)=1</annotation></semantics></math>. Adjacent static frames merge first, and distant shots stay apart. The time coordinate is normalized to <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, independent of frame rate and duration.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.4 </span>Semantic centroids</h3>

<div id="S6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The position features set the partition and then leave the index. Otherwise the inner product with a query would contain a content-independent bias. Given clusters <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}=\{C_{1},\ldots,C_{K}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}=\{C_{1},\ldots,C_{K}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, the centroid uses only the original semantic vectors, <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{v}_{k}=\frac{1}{|C_{k}|}\sum_{i\in C_{k}}\hat{v}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></msub><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{v}_{k}=\frac{1}{|C_{k}|}\sum_{i\in C_{k}}\hat{v}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, and is renormalized:</p>
<table id="S6.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{k}=\frac{\bar{v}_{k}}{\|\bar{v}_{k}\|_{2}}\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{k}=\frac{\bar{v}_{k}}{\|\bar{v}_{k}\|_{2}}\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Because every member is a unit vector,</p>
<table id="S6.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{|C_{k}|}\sum_{i\in C_{k}}\|\hat{v}_{i}-\bar{v}_{k}\|_{2}^{2}=1-\|\bar{v}_{k}\|_{2}^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></munder><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{|C_{k}|}\sum_{i\in C_{k}}\|\hat{v}_{i}-\bar{v}_{k}\|_{2}^{2}=1-\|\bar{v}_{k}\|_{2}^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(21)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.3" class="ltx_p">A more dispersed cluster has a shorter mean. Scoring with <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{v}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>v</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{v}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> would penalize clusters that cover more content. After equation <a href="#S6.E20" title="In 6.4 Semantic centroids ‣ 6 ST-HAC ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a> the inner product is <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\cos\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, which matches the score used during training. Table <a href="#S8.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ 8.5 Compression methods at the same budget ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> compares the two.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.5 </span>Fixed-scale int8 and the bytes in one record</h3>

<div id="S6.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each coordinate of <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> lies in <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, and the corpus shares the scale <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/127" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>127</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/127</annotation></semantics></math>. Indexing rounds at that scale, <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mu}_{k,j}=\operatorname{clip}(\operatorname{round}(127\,\mu_{k,j}),-127,127)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>μ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>clip</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>round</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>127</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>127,127</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mu}_{k,j}=\operatorname{clip}(\operatorname{round}(127\,\mu_{k,j}),-127,127)</annotation></semantics></math>.
The per-coordinate error is at most <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/254" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>254</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/254</annotation></semantics></math>. Scores accumulate in integer arithmetic, and a new record is appended directly. Table <a href="#S9.T17" title="Table 17 ‣ 9.2 Int8 scales ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a> compares the scales. At <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\leq 128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\leq 128</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=64</annotation></semantics></math>, the int8 multi-vectors take at most <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8{,}192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8,192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8{,}192</annotation></semantics></math> bytes, the fp32 mean takes <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math> bytes, and the optional <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>-bit signs take <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,024</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}024</annotation></semantics></math> bytes. The two-level index is at most <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8{,}448" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8,448</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8{,}448</annotation></semantics></math> bytes (<math id="S6.SS5.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.87" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7.87</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.87</annotation></semantics></math> GiB per million records). With the sign bits, the three-stage index is at most <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9{,}472" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9,472</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9{,}472</annotation></semantics></math> bytes (<math id="S6.SS5.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8.82</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.82</annotation></semantics></math> GiB per million records).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Three-stage retrieval</h2>

<section id="S7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.1 </span>Three views of one record</h3>

<div id="S7.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A two-stage pipeline often reads a full-precision side index after the coarse pass, and that side index is hundreds of gigabytes at million scale. OmniEVIE reads all three stages from the record in Section <a href="#S6" title="6 ST-HAC ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> (Figure <a href="#S7.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 7.5 Localizing the hit ‣ 7 Three-stage retrieval ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, Table <a href="#S7.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 7.1 Three views of one record ‣ 7 Three-stage retrieval ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.T6" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6: </span>Candidate representation, operator, and bytes of the three stages. <math id="S7.T6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>K</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of stored centroids, at most <math id="S7.T6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math>.</figcaption>
<table id="S7.T6.6" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S7.T6.6.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S7.T6.6.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S7.T6.6.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Stage</span></th>
<th id="S7.T6.6.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S7.T6.6.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Representation</span></th>
<th id="S7.T6.6.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S7.T6.6.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Operator</span></th>
<th id="S7.T6.6.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S7.T6.6.1.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Window</span></th>
<th id="S7.T6.6.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S7.T6.6.1.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Bytes</span></th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S7.T6.6.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S7.T6.6.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S7.T6.6.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">S1</span></td>
<td id="S7.T6.6.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><math id="S7.T6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{\mathrm{avg}}=\operatorname{L2}(\frac{1}{K^{\prime}}\sum_{k}\mu_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">μ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">avg</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">=</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">L2</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn><msup><mi mathsize="0.900em">K</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">′</mo></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">k</mi></msub><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">μ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{\mathrm{avg}}=\operatorname{L2}(\frac{1}{K^{\prime}}\sum_{k}\mu_{k})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S7.T6.6.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S7.T6.6.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Exact inner product or ANN</span></td>
<td id="S7.T6.6.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><math id="S7.T6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\mathrm{db}}\to N_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">db</mi></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\mathrm{db}}\to N_{1}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S7.T6.6.2.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><math id="S7.T6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn mathsize="0.900em">256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
<tr id="S7.T6.6.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S7.T6.6.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S7.T6.6.3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">S2</span></td>
<td id="S7.T6.6.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><math id="S7.T6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{sign}(\mu_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">sign</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">(</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">μ</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">k</mi></msub><mo maxsize="0.900em" minsize="0.900em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{sign}(\mu_{k})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S7.T6.6.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S7.T6.6.3.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Hamming MaxSim, XOR and popcount</span></td>
<td id="S7.T6.6.3.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><math id="S7.T6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{1}\to N_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mn mathsize="0.900em">2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{1}\to N_{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S7.T6.6.3.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><math id="S7.T6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}024" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn mathsize="0.900em">1,024</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}024</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
<tr id="S7.T6.6.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S7.T6.6.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S7.T6.6.4.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">S3</span></td>
<td id="S7.T6.6.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S7.T6.6.4.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Fixed-scale int8 <math id="S7.T6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\mu}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>μ</mi><mo mathsize="1.110em">^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\mu}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math></span></td>
<td id="S7.T6.6.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><span id="S7.T6.6.4.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Int8 MaxSim, plus equation <a href="#S4.E9" title="In 4.5 Query-side saliency gate and noise floor ‣ 4 Model and training ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a></span></td>
<td id="S7.T6.6.4.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><math id="S7.T6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{2}\to\mathrm{top}\text{-}k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">N</mi><mn mathsize="0.900em">2</mn></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">top</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext mathsize="0.900em">-</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">k</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{2}\to\mathrm{top}\text{-}k</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S7.T6.6.4.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"><math id="S7.T6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8{,}192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn mathsize="0.900em">8,192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8{,}192</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S7.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The query is encoded once, and its mean and sign bits are read from that same output.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.2 </span>Latency and window trade-offs</h3>

<div id="S7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With corpus size <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\mathrm{db}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>db</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\mathrm{db}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{q}</annotation></semantics></math> query tokens, at most <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> centroids, and dimension <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, the retrieval time is</p>
<table id="S7.E22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.E22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\mathrm{total}}=c_{\mathrm{s1}}\,N_{\mathrm{db}}\,d+c_{\mathrm{pop}}\,N_{1}\,L_{q}\,K+c_{\mathrm{int8}}\,N_{2}\,L_{q}\,K." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>total</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>s1</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>db</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>pop</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>int8</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\mathrm{total}}=c_{\mathrm{s1}}\,N_{\mathrm{db}}\,d+c_{\mathrm{pop}}\,N_{1}\,L_{q}\,K+c_{\mathrm{int8}}\,N_{2}\,L_{q}\,K.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(22)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The first term is the S1 scan, the second is Hamming S2, and the third is int8 S3. At <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=64</annotation></semantics></math> the sign pattern of one centroid is one <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math>-bit word, scored by one XOR and one popcount, while the int8 dot product performs <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> multiply-adds. At the median query length and <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=128</annotation></semantics></math>, int8 scoring costs about <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20.0\,\mu\mathrm{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>20.0</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20.0\,\mu\mathrm{s}</annotation></semantics></math> per candidate and Hamming scoring about <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.0\,\mu\mathrm{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4.0</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.0\,\mu\mathrm{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=c_{\mathrm{int8}}/c_{\mathrm{pop}}=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>int8</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>pop</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=c_{\mathrm{int8}}/c_{\mathrm{pop}}=5</annotation></semantics></math>. Holding the sum of S2 and S3 fixed, dropping <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta N_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta N_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> int8 candidates buys</p>
<table id="S7.E23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.E23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta N_{1}=r\,\Delta N_{2}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta N_{1}=r\,\Delta N_{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(23)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">extra candidates in the S1 window. An S1 window that feeds S3 directly stays small, because the int8 score dominates the time. On a larger corpus that fixed window is a smaller fraction of the records, and the mean vector drops the true hit before S3 ever sees it. S2 cuts the int8 window to about a thousand candidates and, by equation <a href="#S7.E23" title="In 7.2 Latency and window trade-offs ‣ 7 Three-stage retrieval ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>, buys about <math id="S7.SS2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> times as many candidates in S1 at a lower total time.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">S2 stores signs on both sides, so one pair is one XOR and one popcount. A floating-point query against a <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>-bit document still costs on the order of an int8 dot product; that row is the last line of Table <a href="#S9.T18" title="Table 18 ‣ 9.3 Latency ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>. Symmetric <math id="S7.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>-bit is the middle stage, and symmetric int8 is the final stage.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.3 </span>Order preservation of the sign stage</h3>

<div id="S7.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">S2 keeps the relevant candidates inside the top <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. S3 produces the final order. Signs keep the orthant of each coordinate. For unit vectors <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u,v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u,v</annotation></semantics></math> and a random rotation <math id="S7.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>,</p>
<table id="S7.E24" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.E24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{1}{d}\langle\operatorname{sign}(Ru),\,\operatorname{sign}(Rv)\rangle\right]=1-\frac{2\theta}{\pi},\qquad\theta=\arccos\langle u,v\rangle." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>d</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>sign</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>sign</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mi>π</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>arccos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{1}{d}\langle\operatorname{sign}(Ru),\,\operatorname{sign}(Rv)\rangle\right]=1-\frac{2\theta}{\pi},\qquad\theta=\arccos\langle u,v\rangle.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(24)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Hamming similarity is monotone in cosine, so the middle stage keeps that order. OmniEVIE takes signs in the original coordinates. Retention of the full-scan top-<math id="S7.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> is reported in Table <a href="#S9.T18" title="Table 18 ‣ 9.3 Latency ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.4 </span>PLAID and MUVERA</h3>

<div id="S7.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">PLAID clusters the corpus into a global codebook and stores residuals in an inverted index <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>]</cite>. MUVERA projects the multi-vectors of a record to one fixed-dimensional encoding and reuses a single-vector index <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>. Table <a href="#S7.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 7.4 PLAID and MUVERA ‣ 7 Three-stage retrieval ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> compares the three as systems that have to be updated. PLAID fits a corpus that can be reclustered. MUVERA fits a stack that already searches single vectors. OmniEVIE fits a corpus that keeps receiving records of different modalities.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.T7" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:70%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 7: </span>Deployment properties of three multi-vector retrieval designs.</figcaption>

<th id="S7.T7.4.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;"></th>
<th id="S7.T7.4.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">
<span id="S7.T7.4.1.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:89.7pt;">

</span></th>
<th id="S7.T7.4.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">
<span id="S7.T7.4.1.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:82.8pt;">
<span id="S7.T7.4.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.T7.4.1.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">MUVERA</span></span>
</span></th>
<th id="S7.T7.4.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">
<span id="S7.T7.4.1.4.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:89.7pt;">
<span id="S7.T7.4.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.T7.4.1.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">OmniEVIE</span></span>

<tbody class="ltx_tbody">

<section id="S7.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.5 </span>Localizing the hit</h3>

<div id="S7.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each centroid corresponds to a set of patches or a time interval. Bounding boxes and time spans are metadata of the source document, and the S3 argmax names the hit.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For a page or an image, the metadata of <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> stores the minimum rectangle of its member patches and the page index. For a high-weight query token, <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{k}=\arg\max_{k}\langle\hat{q}_{i},\hat{\mu}_{k}\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>max</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>q</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>μ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{k}=\arg\max_{k}\langle\hat{q}_{i},\hat{\mu}_{k}\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> highlights that rectangle. The argmax is an intermediate of MaxSim. Localization keeps a cluster whose rectangle covers at most <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the page. A larger rectangle is whitespace and background spread over the page. For a long video, clips are encoded in fixed windows with the same record format, and each centroid stores <math id="S7.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[t_{\min},t_{\max}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[t_{\min},t_{\max}]</annotation></semantics></math>. The windows of one video are placed on a single timeline by video identifier, and the span is the heat of equation <a href="#S7.E25" title="In 7.5 Localizing the hit ‣ 7 Three-stage retrieval ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">25</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The interval hit by one action word covers part of the segment, and the whole segment comes from placing every query token on one time axis. On the QVHighlights validation set, <math id="S7.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>60.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the relevant segments cross a window boundary. Windows are encoded and clustered separately, and a centroid stays inside its window, so each token takes its best centroid in every window and evidence above the noise floor enters the heat on both sides of the boundary. Let <math id="S7.SS5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{i}^{(j)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{i}^{(j)}</annotation></semantics></math> be the maximum similarity of token <math id="S7.SS5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> inside window <math id="S7.SS5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.SS5.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{k}_{i}^{(j)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{k}_{i}^{(j)}</annotation></semantics></math> the corresponding centroid. The heat of group <math id="S7.SS5.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is</p>
<table id="S7.E25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.E25.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="h(g)=\sum_{j=1}^{N_{\mathrm{win}}}\;\sum_{i:\,g\in[t_{\min}(\hat{k}_{i}^{(j)}),\,t_{\max}(\hat{k}_{i}^{(j)})]}w_{i}\operatorname{ReLU}\!\big(r_{i}^{(j)}-\theta_{\mathrm{nf}}\big)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>win</mi></msub></munderover><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.448em">:</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mpadded style="width:2.535em;" width="2.535em"><mi>ReLU</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>nf</mi></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(g)=\sum_{j=1}^{N_{\mathrm{win}}}\;\sum_{i:\,g\in[t_{\min}(\hat{k}_{i}^{(j)}),\,t_{\max}(\hat{k}_{i}^{(j)})]}w_{i}\operatorname{ReLU}\!\big(r_{i}^{(j)}-\theta_{\mathrm{nf}}\big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(25)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.SS5.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Each token adds the part of equation <a href="#S4.E9" title="In 4.5 Query-side saliency gate and noise floor ‣ 4 Model and training ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> above the noise floor, multiplied by the gate weight of equation <a href="#S4.E8" title="In 4.5 Query-side saliency gate and noise floor ‣ 4 Model and training ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, onto the temporal groups of its centroid, and a larger weight contributes more. The group with the highest heat is the located point, and the connected segment where the heat is at least <math id="S7.SS5.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>80</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the peak is the returned span. The ranking score still takes the global maximum of equation <a href="#S4.E9" title="In 4.5 Query-side saliency gate and noise floor ‣ 4 Model and training ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>. Figure <a href="#S9.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 9.5 Evidence localization and video time localization ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> gives the examples, the measurements, and the context passed to the downstream generator.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S7.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.32203v1/figures/fig5_three_stage.png" id="S7.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/167;" width="476" height="167" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>Three-stage retrieval. (a) The candidate window and the time of each stage on one million records. (b) Time per candidate of the three operators, at the median query length and <math id="S7.F6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=128</annotation></semantics></math>. (c) The S2 window <math id="S7.F6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and top-10 retention on the mixed video pool.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">8 </span>Experiments</h2>

<section id="S8.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">8.1 </span>Protocol</h3>

<div id="S8.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unless a row says otherwise, every OmniEVIE number uses <math id="S8.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\leq 128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\leq 128</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S8.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=64</annotation></semantics></math>, and the fixed int8 scale. Task definitions follow MMEB <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>; Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Evaluation suites ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> lists the suites. MMEB-V2 numbers for WeMM-Embedding and Qwen3-VL-Embedding are the official leaderboard results. The MMEB-V3 text and agent numbers for Qwen3-VL-Embedding are taken from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al. [40]</a></cite>. In Table <a href="#S8.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ 8.3 Visual documents, fine-grained images, and video ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> the Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B average is the published ViDoRe V3 number <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite>; the per-domain numbers are our rerun of that setup, and the rerun average is <math id="S8.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58.37" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>58.37</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58.37</annotation></semantics></math>. WeMM-Embedding-9B on MMEB-V3 is the leaderboard value <math id="S8.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="59.33" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>59.33</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">59.33</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">8.2 </span>MMEB-V2 and MMEB-V3</h3>

<div id="S8.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S8.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ 8.2 MMEB-V2 and MMEB-V3 ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> breaks out the text and agent subgroups of MMEB-V3 (190 tasks). Text subgroups are reasoning retrieval (T-RR), instruction following (T-IF), long context (T-LC), multi-condition (T-MC), and general retrieval (T-GR). Agent subgroups are Tool, GUI, Memory, and MCMR. Table <a href="#S8.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ 8.2 MMEB-V2 and MMEB-V3 ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> reports MMEB-V2 (78 tasks) as four families: all, image, video, and visual documents. The full-sequence rows are the blue line in Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1.3 What OmniEVIE does ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:70%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 8: </span>MMEB-V3 over 190 tasks. All is the unweighted mean in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Evaluation suites ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>. Text reports nDCG@5; other groups report Hit@1. The 8-frame row changes only the video frame cap. Bold marks the best value in the column.</figcaption>
