<div id="S8.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">OmniEVIE reaches <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.06</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.06</annotation></semantics></math> on MMEB-V3. With video capped at the official <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> frames the same weights score <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="59.76" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>59.76</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">59.76</annotation></semantics></math>, above the WeMM-Embedding-9B value of <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="59.33" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>59.33</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">59.33</annotation></semantics></math>. MMEB-V2 is <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="77.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>77.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">77.96</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.62" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.62</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.62</annotation></semantics></math> below WeMM-Embedding-9B overall, <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3.78" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3.78</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.78</annotation></semantics></math> on images, and <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.69" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.69</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.69</annotation></semantics></math> on video. Those image and video gaps are in fine-grained classification and video retrieval. The MMEB-V3 gain is on long text: text overall is <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="51.77" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>51.77</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">51.77</annotation></semantics></math>, with instruction following at <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="69.65" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>69.65</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">69.65</annotation></semantics></math>, long context at <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70.71" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>70.71</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70.71</annotation></semantics></math>, and multi-condition retrieval at <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="67.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>67.75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">67.75</annotation></semantics></math>. Agent overall is <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="54.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>54.03</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54.03</annotation></semantics></math>, and tool retrieval is <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="58.84" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>58.84</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">58.84</annotation></semantics></math>. Late interaction matches each query condition to a different span of that text. The released index scores <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>84.02</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84.02</annotation></semantics></math> on visual documents. The highest entry in that column of Table <a href="#S8.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ 8.2 MMEB-V2 and MMEB-V3 ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> is the full sequence at <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S8.SS2.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84.70" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>84.70</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84.70</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>

</figure>
<div id="S8.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In Table <a href="#S8.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ 8.3 Visual documents, fine-grained images, and video ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>, the <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K128\times d64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K128\times d64</annotation></semantics></math> int8 index scores <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="62.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>62.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62.96</annotation></semantics></math> on ViDoRe V3, against <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64.34" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64.34</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64.34</annotation></semantics></math> for the uncompressed <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math> sequence. The compressed index is <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7.87" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>7.87</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7.87</annotation></semantics></math> GiB per million pages, about <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/486" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>486</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/486</annotation></semantics></math> of the fp16 full sequence, and the loss is <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.38" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.38</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.38</annotation></semantics></math> points. Reducing <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> further to <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>, or <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.15</annotation></semantics></math> GiB per million pages, leaves <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="61.16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>61.16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">61.16</annotation></semantics></math>. Computing and energy are the highest domains (<math id="S8.SS3.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="78.73" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>78.73</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78.73</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="69.94" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>69.94</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">69.94</annotation></semantics></math>); French finance and physics are the lowest (<math id="S8.SS3.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="52.52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>52.52</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">52.52</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.SS3.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50.28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50.28</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50.28</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In Table <a href="#S8.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ 8.3 Visual documents, fine-grained images, and video ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>, Top-1 on FORB, Street2Shop, and MovingFashion is <math id="S8.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.94" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>89.94</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.94</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S8.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72.16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>72.16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72.16</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S8.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75.98" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>75.98</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75.98</annotation></semantics></math>. Street2Shop and MovingFashion pair product photos taken in different scenes, so the match is a local part of the product across different scenes. OmniEVIE averages <math id="S8.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="78.74" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>78.74</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78.74</annotation></semantics></math> across the four video datasets. Replacing the native video tokens by an independent encoding of each frame drops that average to <math id="S8.SS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="71.13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>71.13</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">71.13</annotation></semantics></math> and drops forward-versus-reversed accuracy from <math id="S8.SS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75.63\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>75.63</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75.63\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S8.SS3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="51.17\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>51.17</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">51.17\%</annotation></semantics></math>. The forward and reversed clips then produce the same set of vectors, and the accuracy falls to chance.</p>
</div>
</section>

<div id="S8.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Stage 3 is where image, text, and agent move. Adding classification, question answering, and tools takes image from <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="39.33" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>39.33</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">39.33</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75.67" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>75.67</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75.67</annotation></semantics></math>, text from <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="45.74" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>45.74</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">45.74</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50.77" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50.77</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50.77</annotation></semantics></math>, and agent from <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="36.73" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>36.73</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">36.73</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50.85" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>50.85</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50.85</annotation></semantics></math>, while visual documents stay near <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="83" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>83</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">83</annotation></semantics></math>. Against uniform MaxSim, the gate adds <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.36" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.36</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.36</annotation></semantics></math> on agent and <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.28</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.28</annotation></semantics></math> on video; the noise floor then adds <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.68" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.68</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.68</annotation></semantics></math> on agent and <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.15</annotation></semantics></math> on visual documents. Tool and memory candidates are long documents, and a few query tokens decide the score; amplifying the excess above the floor gives those tokens a larger share. Each of the four merge steps operates by parameter addition. Averaging full-data runs from one start adds <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.76" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.76</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.76</annotation></semantics></math> on agent and <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.63" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.63</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.63</annotation></semantics></math> on image. Merging across rounds adds <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.44" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.44</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.44</annotation></semantics></math> on image. The four specialists add <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.49" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.49</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.49</annotation></semantics></math> on agent, <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.36" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.36</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.36</annotation></semantics></math> on video, and <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.27" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.27</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.27</annotation></semantics></math> on image, and visual documents change by <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.32</annotation></semantics></math>. A per-block coefficient, compared with one shared coefficient, adds <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.22" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.22</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.22</annotation></semantics></math> on agent and <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.12</annotation></semantics></math> on video, as equation <a href="#S5.E15" title="In 5.2 Per-block coefficients ‣ 5 Block-wise model merging ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> predicts, and visual documents change by <math id="S8.SS4.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.22" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.22</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.22</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>

<div id="S8.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At the same budget of <math id="S8.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math> int8 vectors of dimension <math id="S8.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math>, ST-HAC scores <math id="S8.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="62.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>62.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62.96</annotation></semantics></math>, the full sequence scores <math id="S8.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="63.09" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>63.09</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">63.09</annotation></semantics></math>, uniform pooling scores <math id="S8.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="56.50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>56.50</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">56.50</annotation></semantics></math>, and random token retention scores <math id="S8.SS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.41" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.41</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.41</annotation></semantics></math>. Two ablations stay within <math id="S8.SS5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.06</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.06</annotation></semantics></math> of ST-HAC: <math id="S8.SS5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{s}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{s}=0</annotation></semantics></math> drops the spatial term from the clustering feature and groups by semantics and time alone (<math id="S8.SS5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="62.90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>62.90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62.90</annotation></semantics></math>), and the raw-mean variant skips the centroid renormalization of equation <a href="#S6.E20" title="In 6.4 Semantic centroids ‣ 6 ST-HAC ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a> and keeps the raw norm of the cluster mean (<math id="S8.SS5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="63.00" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>63.00</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">63.00</annotation></semantics></math>). Building the index takes about <math id="S8.SS5.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20.0</annotation></semantics></math> single-thread milliseconds per page. Records are split across processes: one hundred million pages take about <math id="S8.SS5.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\times 10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times 10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> single-thread seconds, or about <math id="S8.SS5.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math> hours over <math id="S8.SS5.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> processes, and a new record is appended directly.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">8.6 </span>Business scenarios</h3>

<div id="S8.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond the public benchmarks, we evaluate on real business scenarios (finance, industry, museums, landmarks, and automotive) covering text-to-image, image-to-image, and combined image-text retrieval; the scenario names are generalized and do not map to specific data sources. Table <a href="#S8.T14" title="Table 14 ‣ 8.6 Business scenarios ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> reports Top-1 against two strong business baselines, Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B and WeMM-Embedding-9B.</p>

<div id="S8.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">On the category means OmniEVIE is first on all three: text-to-image <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64.2</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="61.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>61.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">61.2</annotation></semantics></math>, image-to-image <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>96.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.5</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>94.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">94.1</annotation></semantics></math>, and image-text <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>90.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90.4</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>84.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84.1</annotation></semantics></math>. Among representative scenarios, finance, industry, and museums in text-to-image reach <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>76.3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76.3</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="81.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>81.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">81.8</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="79.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>79.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">79.2</annotation></semantics></math>, which are <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.9</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.9</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11.7</annotation></semantics></math> points above the <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math>B baseline; landmarks in image-to-image reach <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="92.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>92.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">92.9</annotation></semantics></math>, a gain of <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="11.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>11.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11.5</annotation></semantics></math>; and automotive in image-text reaches <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100.0</annotation></semantics></math>, a gain of <math id="S8.SS6.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.1</annotation></semantics></math>. The gains are largest where matching needs layout detail or a local product feature, consistent with the public-set results above.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S9" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">9 </span>Analysis</h2>

<section id="S9.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">9.1 </span>Two degrees of freedom in the byte budget</h3>

<div id="S9.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At a fixed number of bytes the index can keep more vectors <math id="S9.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> or a higher dimension <math id="S9.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>. Table <a href="#S9.T15" title="Table 15 ‣ 9.1 Two degrees of freedom in the byte budget ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> separates the two choices. The first rows are the full Prefix-MRL sequence at each width. The last comparison holds the multi-vector payload at <math id="S9.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4{,}096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4,096</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4{,}096</annotation></semantics></math> bytes and asks whether <math id="S9.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=64,d=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=64,d=64</annotation></semantics></math> beats <math id="S9.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=32,d=128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=32,d=128</annotation></semantics></math>. Section 1 says the count decides how many local pieces can be matched at once, while the dimension decides how well one vector separates lookalikes. When the evidence is scattered, the count should matter more.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7: </span>Storage against ViDoRe V3 accuracy for the Prefix-MRL width and the ST-HAC budget, per million records on a log axis. The gray square and triangle are the single-vector baseline Qwen3-VL-Embedding-8B and the multi-vector baseline Nemotron-ColEmbed-V2-8B, placed at their own index storage (the latter at <math id="S9.F7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4096</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4096</annotation></semantics></math> dimensions and about <math id="S9.F7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="773" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>773</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">773</annotation></semantics></math> tokens per page, about <math id="S9.F7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5{,}898" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5,898</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5{,}898</annotation></semantics></math> GiB per million in fp16); marker size reflects the roughly <math id="S9.F7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>B model scale, larger than the <math id="S9.F7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.5</annotation></semantics></math>B of OmniEVIE.</figcaption>

<div id="S9.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Figure <a href="#S9.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ 9.1 Two degrees of freedom in the byte budget ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> and Table <a href="#S9.T15" title="Table 15 ‣ 9.1 Two degrees of freedom in the byte budget ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>, cutting the full sequence from dimension <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2048</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>512</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">512</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> yields <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64.34" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64.34</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64.34</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64.12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64.12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64.12</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="63.55" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>63.55</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">63.55</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="63.09" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>63.09</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">63.09</annotation></semantics></math>. A <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="32\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32\times</annotation></semantics></math> cut in storage costs <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.25</annotation></semantics></math> points, so most of the full-sequence score survives a much narrower vector. At a payload of <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4{,}096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4,096</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4{,}096</annotation></semantics></math> bytes, <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=64,d=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=64,d=64</annotation></semantics></math> scores <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="62.47" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>62.47</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62.47</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=32,d=128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=32,d=128</annotation></semantics></math> scores <math id="S9.SS1.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="61.82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>61.82</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">61.82</annotation></semantics></math>. Spending the bytes on more vectors beats spending them on a higher dimension.</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">On MMEB the same comparison uses the full <math id="S9.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math> sequence, the blue line in Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1.3 What OmniEVIE does ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, as the 190-task mean in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Evaluation suites ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> (Table <a href="#S9.T16" title="Table 16 ‣ 9.1 Two degrees of freedom in the byte budget ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a>). The released index scores <math id="S9.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.06</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.06</annotation></semantics></math> on V3, <math id="S9.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.62" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.62</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.62</annotation></semantics></math> below the ceiling of <math id="S9.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.68" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.68</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.68</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S9.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="77.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>77.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">77.96</annotation></semantics></math> on V2, <math id="S9.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.60</annotation></semantics></math> below <math id="S9.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="78.56" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>78.56</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78.56</annotation></semantics></math>. A full sequence cut to <math id="S9.SS1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=64</annotation></semantics></math> scores <math id="S9.SS1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="59.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>59.02</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">59.02</annotation></semantics></math> on V3, below the released index.</p>

<p id="S9.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The fixed scale scores <math id="S9.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="62.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>62.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62.96</annotation></semantics></math>, within <math id="S9.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.03</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.03</annotation></semantics></math> of fp16 centroids (<math id="S9.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="62.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>62.99</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62.99</annotation></semantics></math>), a per-vector fp16 scale (<math id="S9.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="62.96" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>62.96</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62.96</annotation></semantics></math>), and a corpus-wide scale (<math id="S9.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="62.97" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>62.97</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">62.97</annotation></semantics></math>). Dropping the scale falls to <math id="S9.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="57.82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>57.82</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57.82</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<section id="S9.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">9.3 </span>Latency</h3>

<div id="S9.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S9.T18" title="Table 18 ‣ 9.3 Latency ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a> reports single-thread CPU retrieval time at three corpus sizes. The operating point is <math id="S9.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{1}=5{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5,000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{1}=5{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{2}=1{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1,000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{2}=1{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>. Deltas and top-10 retention are measured against full int8 MaxSim on a ViDoRe V3 pool of <math id="S9.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19{,}252" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19,252</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19{,}252</annotation></semantics></math> pages and a video pool of <math id="S9.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="13{,}932" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>13,932</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13{,}932</annotation></semantics></math> clips. Table <a href="#S9.T19" title="Table 19 ‣ 9.3 Latency ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a> varies the query length on the one-million corpus.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S9.T18" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 18: </span>Single-thread retrieval latency in milliseconds. Cells are totals. <math id="S9.T18.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> is the nDCG@10 change on the document pool and the video pool.</figcaption>
<table id="S9.T18.5" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">

The same windows at <math id="S9.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{2}=200" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{2}=200</annotation></semantics></math> retain <math id="S9.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98.5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>98.5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.5\%</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="85.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>85.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">85.7\%</annotation></semantics></math>. <div id="S9.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">On one million records the operating point takes <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="54.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>54.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54.2</annotation></semantics></math> ms, of which S1, S2, and S3 take <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>14.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14.6</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.7</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.9</annotation></semantics></math> ms. Full int8 MaxSim takes <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12{,}781" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12,781</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12{,}781</annotation></semantics></math> ms, so the three-stage path is <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="236\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>236</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">236\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster, and nDCG@10 changes by <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.13" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.13</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.13</annotation></semantics></math> on documents and <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.26" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.26</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.26</annotation></semantics></math> on video. The same split is <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.5</annotation></semantics></math> / <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>19.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.6</annotation></semantics></math> / <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20.8</annotation></semantics></math> ms at <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> thousand records. At five million records S1 grows to <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>80.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80.5</annotation></semantics></math> ms, because it scans the whole corpus, and the total is <math id="S9.SS3.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="120.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>120.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">120.2</annotation></semantics></math> ms.</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">S1 is a <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional scan, so the same comparison also favors OmniEVIE over an exact high-dimensional single vector once the corpus is large. At <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> thousand records, <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=4096</annotation></semantics></math> take <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="34.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>34.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">34.6</annotation></semantics></math> ms and <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.9</annotation></semantics></math> ms, close to the three-stage total. At one million records they take <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="331.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>331.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">331.0</annotation></semantics></math> ms and <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="604.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>604.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">604.0</annotation></semantics></math> ms, against <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="54.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>54.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54.2</annotation></semantics></math> ms (<math id="S9.SS3.p4.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="6.1\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.1\times</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="11.1\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>11.1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11.1\times</annotation></semantics></math>). At five million records they take <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}666" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,666</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}666</annotation></semantics></math> ms and <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{,}039" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3,039</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{,}039</annotation></semantics></math> ms, against <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="120.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>120.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">120.2</annotation></semantics></math> ms (<math id="S9.SS3.p4.m15" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="13.9\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>13.9</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13.9\times</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m16" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="25.3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25.3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25.3\times</annotation></semantics></math>). The two-stage pipeline at a similar latency, <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{1}=2{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2,000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{1}=2{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="55.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>55.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">55.2</annotation></semantics></math> ms, drops nDCG by <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.60</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.66" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.66</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.66</annotation></semantics></math>. The two-stage pipeline with a similar accuracy, <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{1}=5{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5,000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{1}=5{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>, takes <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="115.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>115.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">115.1</annotation></semantics></math> ms. S1 is constant in the query length. S2 and S3 grow with it. A query of about <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="400" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>400</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">400</annotation></semantics></math> tokens takes <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="439.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>439.9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">439.9</annotation></semantics></math> ms and is still <math id="S9.SS3.p4.m25" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="29\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>29</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">29\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster than full int8 MaxSim.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S9.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">9.4 </span>Token alignment and gate weights</h3>

<div id="S9.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A single vector returns one scalar. The multi-vector index shows which part of the candidate each token hits. Figure <a href="#S9.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 9.4 Token alignment and gate weights ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> uses one medical query from ViDoRe V3: “Did the FDA’s 2018 Strategic Policy Roadmap eliminate the need for clinical trials in biosimilar approval processes?” The tokens Strategic, Policy, and Road each hit the cluster of the matching word in the bold title. Those clusters contain <math id="S9.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S9.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math> patches, and the maximum similarity is above <math id="S9.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.94" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.94</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.94</annotation></semantics></math>. The gate lifts these three tokens above the uniform weight and puts the last <math id="S9.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> expansion tokens below it. On the relevant page every token is above the noise floor, with mean <math id="S9.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.82" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.82</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.82</annotation></semantics></math>. On an unrelated page from the same domain the mean is <math id="S9.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.43</annotation></semantics></math>, and about half of the tokens fall below the floor. A word that appears on both pages, such as FDA, still matches. Equation (<a href="#S4.E9" title="In 4.5 Query-side saliency gate and noise floor ‣ 4 Model and training ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>) amplifies the excess above <math id="S9.SS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.38" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.38</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.38</annotation></semantics></math>, and a token below the floor keeps its original value.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S9.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.32203v1/figures/fig7_alignment.png" id="S9.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:429/368;" width="429" height="368" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8: </span>Per-token hits and query-side gate weights. (a)(b) Member patches of the clusters hit by three query words on a medical document page from ViDoRe V3, with each cluster colored separately. (c) Per-token weights from the salience gate, with the dashed line marking the uniform weight. (d) Per-token maximum similarity on the relevant page versus an unrelated same-domain page, with the dashed line at the noise floor <math id="S9.F8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{\mathrm{nf}}=0.38" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>nf</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.38</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{\mathrm{nf}}=0.38</annotation></semantics></math>.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S9.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">9.5 </span>Evidence localization and video time localization</h3>

<div id="S9.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The same argmax places the hit on a page region or a video time (Section <a href="#S7.SS5" title="7.5 Localizing the hit ‣ 7 Three-stage retrieval ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7.5</span></a>). In Figure <a href="#S9.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 9.5 Evidence localization and video time localization ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>(a)(b)(c), three ViDoRe V3 queries hit the answer on the page ranked first by S3: Denmark hits the DK row and contracts hits the column header; the page in (b) is French, where percentage hits “3 %” and photovoltaic hits “photovoltaïque totale” in the same sentence; in (c), 2014 hits the 2014 column of the bar chart and Therapy hits the chart title.</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S9.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 9.5 Evidence localization and video time localization ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>(d) is a <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="150" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>150</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">150</annotation></semantics></math> s QVHighlights video <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite>, encoded in <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> windows. The labeled segment of <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="66" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>66</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">66</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S9.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90</annotation></semantics></math> s crosses the window boundary at <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75</annotation></semantics></math> s. Couch scores <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.77" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.77</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.77</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.69" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.69</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.69</annotation></semantics></math> on the two sides and hosts scores <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.74" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.74</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.74</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.57</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.57</annotation></semantics></math>, all above the noise floor, so equation <a href="#S7.E25" title="In 7.5 Localizing the hit ‣ 7 Three-stage retrieval ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">25</span></a> adds them; news hits another shot at <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S9.SS5.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="38" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>38</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">38</annotation></semantics></math> s. The heat peaks at <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="77" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>77</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">77</annotation></semantics></math> s, and the returned span of <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S9.SS5.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>94</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">94</annotation></semantics></math> s overlaps the label and runs <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> s past it. Over all <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}083" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,083</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}083</annotation></semantics></math> queries, the peak falls inside the label for <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="78.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>78.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> and the span intersects it for <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>94.3</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">94.3\%</annotation></semantics></math>. The span averages <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="27.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>27.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27.7</annotation></semantics></math> s, <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="18\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>18</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">18\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the video, against <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="44.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>44.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">44.9\%</annotation></semantics></math> for a random span of the same length and <math id="S9.SS5.p2.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>24.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> for a random point (Figure <a href="#S9.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 9.5 Evidence localization and video time localization ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>(e)).</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A global vector returns the whole video or the whole page, so a question about which second or which part of the page still sends that whole video or page to the downstream generator. An OmniEVIE hit carries its place: a bounding rectangle for a page or an image, and the returned span of equation <a href="#S7.E25" title="In 7.5 Localizing the hit ‣ 7 Three-stage retrieval ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">25</span></a> for a video. The downstream generator reads only that rectangle or that span; Figure <a href="#S9.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 9.5 Evidence localization and video time localization ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>(a) passes the row for DK, and Figure <a href="#S9.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 9.5 Evidence localization and video time localization ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>(d) passes <math id="S9.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>75</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">75</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S9.SS5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="94" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>94</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">94</annotation></semantics></math> s. The video side also needs no video parsing model. A common long-video pipeline first runs a video understanding model to transcribe each segment into timestamped captions and then retrieves over the text. OmniEVIE encodes the sampled frames directly and takes the time interval of each centroid from the frame indices, so neither indexing nor localization goes through transcription; this is a native route to video retrieval. A long video is stored as fixed windows, one record per window, and equation <a href="#S7.E25" title="In 7.5 Localizing the hit ‣ 7 Three-stage retrieval ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">25</span></a> returns the start and end of the matched segment on the full video timeline.</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SS5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S9.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ 9.5 Evidence localization and video time localization ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> shows three QVHighlights queries, with the middle frames of each row taken from the returned span and the side frames from outside it. In (a), closing a packed suitcase, the label is <math id="S9.SS5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S9.SS5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math> s, the span is <math id="S9.SS5.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="23" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>23</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">23</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S9.SS5.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="38" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>38</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">38</annotation></semantics></math> s, and the peak is at <math id="S9.SS5.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="26" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>26</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">26</annotation></semantics></math> s, where she presses the clothes down into the case; outside are a close view of the bag, her facing the camera, a close-up of her face, and the two of them in a car. In (b), dolls in a display case, the label and the span are both <math id="S9.SS5.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>84</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S9.SS5.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>98</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98</annotation></semantics></math> s with the peak at <math id="S9.SS5.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="87" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>87</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">87</annotation></semantics></math> s; the case fills the span, and the sides show a banquet hall, piled goods, a top-down view of a circular floor pattern, and a selfie of the woman. In (c), a man in a blue shirt driving a yellow car, the label is <math id="S9.SS5.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="118" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>118</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">118</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S9.SS5.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="136" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>136</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">136</annotation></semantics></math> s, the span is <math id="S9.SS5.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="117" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>117</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">117</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S9.SS5.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="136" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>136</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">136</annotation></semantics></math> s, and the peak is at <math id="S9.SS5.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="120" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>120</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">120</annotation></semantics></math> s; the span shows the driver from the back seat, and the sides are the same woman’s selfies.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S9.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.32203v1/figures/fig8_localization.png" id="S9.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/277;" width="429" height="277" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 9: </span>Localized evidence. (a)(b)(c) Clusters hit on the top-ranked page: one color is one cluster, the box is its bounding rectangle, and the bold query words match the boxes. (d) Timestamp lookup in a <math id="S9.F9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="150" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>150</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">150</annotation></semantics></math> s video: bars are each query word’s best centroid in each window, shaded by the margin over the noise floor; the curve is the heat of equation <a href="#S7.E25" title="In 7.5 Localizing the hit ‣ 7 Three-stage retrieval ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">25</span></a>, the band is the labeled segment, and the outlined bar is the returned span. (e) Hit rate of the peak and of the returned span, against a random span of the same length.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S9.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.32203v1/figures/fig9_video_cases.png" id="S9.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/225;" width="429" height="225" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 10: </span>Returned spans for three QVHighlights queries. The outlined middle frames come from the returned span and the gray side frames come from outside it; the number under a frame is its time and the dots mark these frames. The bar is the returned span, the dashed box is the labeled segment, and the triangle is the heat peak. (a) Closing a suitcase. (b) Dolls in a display case. (c) Driving the yellow car.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S9.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">9.6 </span>Limitations</h3>

<div id="S9.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A clip of a few seconds, sampled at a low frame rate, collapses to a handful of temporal groups under the stride of <math id="S9.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, so little of the action remains. The frame rate can be chosen from the length of the clip. Reasoning retrieval, GUI, and memory are still the lowest text and agent subgroups; they need multi-step reasoning retrieval data and interface screenshots. The gate and the noise floor are computed inside S3, so their cost grows linearly with <math id="S9.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{q}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S10" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">10 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OmniEVIE serves text, images, documents, video, and tools from one <math id="S10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.5</annotation></semantics></math>B model and one index. MMEB-V3 is <math id="S10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.06</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.06</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S10.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.62" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.62</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.62</annotation></semantics></math> below the full <math id="S10.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=2048</annotation></semantics></math> sequence at <math id="S10.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60.68" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60.68</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60.68</annotation></semantics></math> on the same 190 tasks. A record is at most <math id="S10.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9{,}472" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9,472</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9{,}472</annotation></semantics></math> bytes, about <math id="S10.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8.8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8.8</annotation></semantics></math> GiB per million records. On one million and five million records, a single thread takes <math id="S10.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="54.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>54.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54.2</annotation></semantics></math> ms and <math id="S10.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="120.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>120.2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">120.2</annotation></semantics></math> ms, <math id="S10.p1.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="11.1\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>11.1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">11.1\times</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.p1.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="25.3\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25.3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25.3\times</annotation></semantics></math> faster than exact search over a <math id="S10.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4096</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4096</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional vector. Search uses the compressed index. The hit names a page region or a video interval.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Training and search use the same score. Evidence grades decide which negatives are false. Candidates are clustered during training into the vectors that will be stored. Specialists trained separately are merged by parameter block, and each block receives its own coefficient. Online, the score is an inner product, a popcount, or an int8 dot product.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.p3.1" class="ltx_p">An agent that retrieves several times in one task benefits when each hit already names its evidence: the generator then reads that region or interval (Figure <a href="#S9.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ 9.5 Evidence localization and video time localization ‣ 9 Analysis ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>). This release tests the architecture, the schedule, and the compressed index on public data: <math id="S10.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>57</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57</annotation></semantics></math> datasets and about <math id="S10.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>M samples. The next stage adds domain data, extends the same record to audio and to long mixed documents, and passes the localized region or interval to a generator. At larger scale the mean vector can itself be quantized or placed in a graph index.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Weights are at <a href="https://huggingface.co/tencent/OmniEVIE-4B" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://huggingface.co/tencent/OmniEVIE-4B</a>. Inference, indexing, and the three-stage retriever are at <a href="https://github.com/Tencent/OmniEVIE" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/Tencent/OmniEVIE</a>. The corpora are public benchmarks and licensed document, image, and video collections. The evidence check filters sensitive material and personally identifiable information. Hyperparameters and evaluation suites are listed in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Hyperparameters ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> and Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Evaluation suites ‣ OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Video in the fine-grained suite is encoded at <math id="A2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> frame per second, at most <math id="A2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> frames, as one native sequence.</p>
